lead.headline: Isaias strengthens to 110 mph ahead of Gulf Coast landfall tonight
lead.dek: Mandatory evacuations in two Florida counties and three Alabama beach towns; surge of 5 to 7 feet forecast from Dauphin Island to Indian Pass
body: Hurricane Isaias strengthened to 110 mph early Friday, just short of major-hurricane strength, and was moving north-northeast at 15 mph about 200 miles south-southeast of the mouth of the Mississippi River, the National Hurricane Center said at 4 a.m. CDT. It is forecast to come ashore between Ocean Springs, Miss., and Florida's Bay County tonight or early Saturday.

The center said Isaias is likely to become a major hurricane this morning, with slight weakening before landfall. It forecast a peak surge of 5 to 7 feet from Dauphin Island, Ala., to Indian Pass, Fla., and 4 to 8 inches of rain, locally 15, across southern Alabama, the Florida Panhandle and Big Bend, with up to 10 inches possible in the Southern Appalachians.

Florida ordered mandatory evacuations in parts of Okaloosa and Walton counties, Alabama ordered non-residents out of Gulf Shores, Orange Beach and Dauphin Island, and Florida, Alabama and Georgia declared emergencies, CBS News and NPR reported. Nearly two-thirds of Gulf oil production had been shut in by noon Thursday, NBC News reported, citing federal regulators.

briefs.headline: ICE officer shoots man in car with 5-year-old in Manhattan
briefs.summary: An ICE agent fired seven rounds and hit a 28-year-old man in the neck at a Marble Hill stop Thursday, NYPD Commissioner Jessica Tisch said; the man is stable and the child was unhurt.

briefs.headline: Prosecutors seek indictment of Jan. 6 witness Cassidy Hutchinson
briefs.summary: Prosecutors have put evidence before a Washington grand jury on whether the former Meadows aide lied to Congress in her 2022 testimony, two sources told CBS News.

briefs.headline: Trump administration suspends Microsoft from green card program
briefs.summary: Vice President JD Vance said Thursday Microsoft is barred from the labor certification program after cutting 6,000 U.S. jobs while obtaining 6,300 visas; Microsoft said 80% of filings covered existing staff.

briefs.headline: Trump says U.S. will not strike Iran before Nov. 3 midterms
briefs.summary: Trump posted late Thursday that the U.S. is in 'productive discussions' with Iran and will not attack before the elections; Brent crude still closed up 4% at $104.28, NBC News reported.

briefs.headline: Navi Pillay wins 2026 Nobel Peace Prize
briefs.summary: The Norwegian Nobel Committee gave the 125th peace prize to the 85-year-old South African jurist and ex-UN rights chief for work ensuring war crimes and genocide are prosecuted.

briefs.headline: Two tankers hit outside Strait of Hormuz within 24 hours
briefs.summary: UKMTO said projectiles hit the tanker Acers 51 nautical miles off Qatar Wednesday; a second tanker burned off Fujairah Thursday. Iran claimed neither, Euronews reported.

briefs.headline: Brazil judge orders arrest of Eduardo Bolsonaro
briefs.summary: Justice Alexandre de Moraes ordered Flavio Bolsonaro's Texas-based brother to begin a four-year sentence and canceled his passport 16 days before the Oct. 25 runoff, AP reported.

briefs.headline: South Africa pulls asylum directive after riots
briefs.summary: Home Affairs halted a court-ordered asylum processing rule after rioters torched 14 cars in Durban and 10 in Soweto and looted foreign-owned shops, DW reported.

briefs.headline: Panther Creek to idle Kanawha surface mine, cut 109 jobs
briefs.summary: Panther Creek Mining filed a WARN notice to shut the Samples Surface Mine and Toms Fork prep plant near Eskdale, cutting 109 jobs starting Dec. 5.

briefs.headline: Morrisey energy and infrastructure chief Johnston exits
briefs.summary: Todd Johnston, the governor's deputy chief of staff and energy, infrastructure and competitiveness director, confirmed Thursday he is leaving for a job in Washington.

briefs.headline: FEMA issues final denial for Boone, Logan flood aid
briefs.summary: WOWK reported Thursday night, citing a denial letter it obtained, that FEMA finally denied a major disaster declaration for June flooding in Boone and Logan counties.

briefs.headline: Boone board votes to close Van high school, Whitesville Elementary
briefs.summary: The Boone County school board voted Thursday to close Van Junior/Senior High and Whitesville Elementary after this school year; Van students would move to Scott High.

regional.item: Police seized over $1.5M in drugs, including 15.5 pounds of cocaine, from a suspected cartel-linked stash house in Barboursville.
The $26M Capital Connector riverfront project along Kanawha Boulevard is going out to bid for construction.
U.S. Marshals offered a $5,000 reward for Gabriel Hargus, 49, of Mineral Wells, a sex offender wanted on federal and state warrants.
Donors turned out Thursday for day one of the two-day Lt. Aaron Acree memorial blood drive in Summersville, which aims for 102 donations.

away.item: A second Common Sense PAC mailer, this one attacking Sen. Rob Plunkett, drew two attorney general complaints this week, the Banner said.

hotspots.item: Webster County football beat Wirt County 20-13 on Friday, Oct. 2, its first win in five tries against the Tigers; the 4-2 Highlanders are off until Oct. 16.
A leaking underground propane tank cut northbound U.S. 17 to one lane at Scotts Hill on Wednesday until a hazmat crew burned it off; all lanes reopened that day.

briefs.headline: Northern Health reports flu cases rising across the north
briefs.summary: Medical health officer Dr. Rakel Kling said lab reports show influenza circulating in the north; flu shot shipments should reach clinics next week.

briefs.headline: Free transit in Prince George on Oct. 17 election day
briefs.summary: B.C. Transit said buses and handyDART will be free Oct. 17 in more than 30 communities, including Prince George. Eight city polls open 8 a.m. to 8 p.m.

briefs.headline: Ousted B.C. Conservative Agou apologizes, will run as independent
briefs.summary: Lorne Doerkson dropped the Victoria-Beacon Hill candidate Thursday over posts the NDP called racist, including one saying a car that hit protesters "should have reversed."
briefs.source: The Canadian Press via CKPG Today

briefs.headline: Doerkson pitches $32,000 tax-free threshold as Eby freezes ICBC rates
briefs.summary: The Conservatives would raise the basic personal amount from $13,216, about $1,000 a year for a $40,000 earner; the NDP put the cost at $2.5B. Eby promised an ICBC rate freeze.

briefs.headline: Ottawa launches $2B heat pump rebate for up to 820,000 homes
briefs.summary: Rebates of up to $10,000 for households below their province's median income, and $2,000 above it, begin early next year, Carney said in Sherbrooke, Que.

briefs.headline: Cold Lake First Nations seeks review of Pacific Link designation
briefs.summary: The Alberta nation asked Federal Court on Thursday to quash Ottawa's national-interest designation of the oil pipeline to B.C., saying it was left out of consultations.

briefs.headline: Crew-12 splashes down off Los Angeles after 237 days
briefs.summary: Dragon landed at 11:34 a.m. ET Thursday with Jessica Meir, Jack Hathaway, Sophie Adenot and Andrey Fedyaev; Meir's 440 career days rank in NASA's top 10.

briefs.headline: Webb watches water clouds shift on coldest brown dwarf
briefs.summary: University of Arizona astronomers saw clouds on WISE 0855, 7.5 light-years away, thicken and thin over 11 hours of Webb spectra, a first beyond the solar system.

briefs.headline: HPV shot before pregnancy tied to fewer preterm births
briefs.summary: A Karolinska study of 624,000 Swedish births in The BMJ found a 5% lower risk of delivery before 37 weeks in vaccinated mothers. The design is observational.

briefs.headline: Ozone and nitrogen oxides blunt pollinators' sense of smell
briefs.summary: A University of Reading review of 22 experiments found ozone cut pollinator performance 42%, nitrogen oxides 46% and the two combined 68%.

briefs.headline: White House summit pledges $2.4B in AI compute for science
briefs.summary: The White House said 11 firms, led by Nvidia at $1B and AMD at $500M, committed compute to the Genesis Mission at Thursday's summit; the figures are the White House's.

briefs.headline: Zenity says one prompt exposed every AWS AgentCore agent
briefs.summary: Zenity Labs said a public agent on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore could leak credentials and alter other agents in the account; it says AWS cut default permissions Sept. 29.

briefs.headline: Fired OpenAI safety researchers dispute misconduct claims
briefs.summary: Jasmine Wang, Tomek Korbak and Mikita Balesni said in an open letter Thursday they did not mishandle data; OpenAI said it found a 'pattern of misconduct,' TechCrunch reported.

kicker: Summers-New River carries no regional line today; Hinton's 60th Railroad Days runs through Sunday.

art.caption: A mooring line doubled over a dock cleat at a Mississippi marina Thursday as boat owners moved out ahead of Isaias.
